narration: In the autumn of AD 79 the mountain above the city of Pompeii opened. A column of ash and pumice rose twenty miles into the sky. Roof tiles broke under the weight of the falling stone. A fleet commander sailed his ships toward the coast to take people off the beach. Ash filled the water and the harbour became too shallow for the boats. A surge of hot gas ran down the slope faster than anyone could walk. The bodies left cavities in the hardened ash that held their exact shape. An archaeologist poured plaster into the cavities eighteen centuries later. A loaf of bread was found still inside a bakery oven. The city had been sitting under six metres of stone the whole time.
